newsitem.title: USA: Burlington Northern sells lines to RailAmerica.
newsitem.headline: Burlington Northern sells lines to RailAmerica.

text.p: Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp said Monday it had sold a cluster of rail lines in and around Crookston, Minn., to Minnesota Northern Railroad Inc, a newly formed subsidiary of RailAmerica Inc.

Effective today, Minnesota Northern Railroad began operations over 241 miles of track, including 37 miles of trackage rights, with traffic from these lines interchanged with Burlington Northern at Burlington Northern's Crookston yard. Minnesota Northern Railroad set up its general offices at Crookston.

These lines, serving northwestern Minnesota, extend north to Warroad near the Canadian border and as far south as Perley near Fargo, N.D.. Rail traffic handled on these lines consists of agricultural products, primarily grains and fertilizer, as well as aggregates and coal. These lines currently handle about 11,000 carloads a year.
The lines were offered for sale in September as part of Burlington Northern's continuing asset evaluation program.
Burlington Northern operates the largest railroad system in the United States with about 31,000 route miles reaching across 27 states and two Canadian provinces.
Since becoming a public company in 1992, RailAmerica has been actively pursuing the acquisition of rail lines throughout the United States and Canada.
